q: The analysis shows that GenAI lowers the cost of producing plausible code while increasing the importance of intent specification, context curation
r: IC1: qualitative thematic analysis of public discourse on GenAI and software engineering; neither an SDD approach, a context mechanism nor an agent evaluation.

q: It proposes Agentic Agile-V, a process framework that uses Agile-V as the lifecycle backbone and a task-level SCOPE-V loop
r: Include: conceptual process framework that turns intent into structured specification artifacts and acceptance evidence for coding agents (group a).

q: We propose CodeSpec, a dual-specification approach for agentic long-horizon feature development.
r: Include: specification-guided agentic feature development with executable architecture and behaviour specifications (group a, not narrowed by EC5).

q: We propose the first agentic pipeline that explicitly decouples behavioral specification elicitation from code synthesis
r: Include: spec agent writes SPEC.md before a code-synthesis agent builds the program, a specification-first agent workflow (group a).

q: we compare five specification formats across three quality dimensions
r: Include: controlled factorial comparison (5 formats x 6 models, 90 trials, cost and quality metrics) of architecture specification formats given to coding agents.

q: we study the effects of different task specifications on agentic token spend with the Kimi K3 model at three thinking efforts
r: Include: measures how Spec Kit-derived task specifications affect agent token cost with 15 repeats; evaluation-method contribution, specification effect on cost (RQ2, RQ4); borderline group c issue-repair tasks.

q: The workflow structures agent-assisted development into four phases where human effort is front-loaded and delegation increases as artifacts mature.
r: Include: phased research-plan-task-implement workflow with artifacts, human review points and context management for coding agents (short industry paper, not EC3).

q: We examine these questions through an exploratory review of practitioner literature.
r: IC1: vision paper on regenerating disposable implementations; no SDD approach, context mechanism or agent evaluation is described or tested.

q: we compared the proposed method with a baseline approach based on a specification-driven development tool (GitHub Spec Kit)
sec: V. Case Study, A. Evaluation Design
r: Include: governed execution harness for LLM code generation compared against a Spec Kit SDD baseline under the same requirements and model (group a).

q: This paper presents Spec-Driven AI, a multiagent framework for specification-centric Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) automation.
r: Include: spec-driven multi-agent SDLC framework with human gates and artifacts; tool demo paper but a full SDD approach (group a).
